# Sprints

<!-- auto-generated by cmd/docgen — do not edit -->

Sprints are time-boxed iterations in Jira Software (Scrum boards). Each sprint
belongs to a board. Sprint IDs are numeric.

## jira sprint list

List sprints for a board.

**Alias:** `ls`

### Usage

```
jira sprint list [flags]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Short | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--board` | `-b` | Board ID (defaults to context board) |
| `--state` | `-s` | Filter by state: `active`, `future`, `closed` (default `active,future`) |
| `--limit` | `-L` | Maximum sprints to display |

### Inherited Flags

| Flag | Short | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--context` | `-c` | Active Jira context name |
| `--json` | | Output in JSON format |
| `--yaml` | | Output in YAML format |

### Examples

```bash
jira sprint list
jira sprint list --board 42
jira sprint list --state active --json
jira sprint list --state closed --limit 5
```

---

## jira sprint view

Display details for a sprint including its dates, goal, and state.

### Usage

```
jira sprint view <sprint-id> [flags]
```

### Examples

```bash
jira sprint view 123
jira sprint view 123 --json
```

---

## jira sprint issues

List all issues in a sprint.

### Usage

```
jira sprint issues <sprint-id> [flags]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Short | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--status` | `-s` | Filter by status |
| `--type` | `-T` | Filter by issue type |
| `--assignee` | `-a` | Filter by assignee |
| `--limit` | `-L` | Maximum issues to display |

### Examples

```bash
jira sprint issues 123
jira sprint issues 123 --status "In Progress"
jira sprint issues 123 --assignee me --json
```

---

## jira sprint add

Add an issue to a sprint.

**Alias:** `jira issue sprint add`

### Usage

```
jira sprint add <issue-key> [flags]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Short | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--sprint` | | Sprint ID or `current` for the active sprint |
| `--board` | `-b` | Board ID (to resolve `current` sprint) |

### Examples

```bash
jira sprint add MYPROJ-42 --sprint 123
jira sprint add MYPROJ-42 --sprint current --board 10
```

---

## jira sprint remove

Remove an issue from its sprint (move to backlog).

**Alias:** `jira issue sprint remove`

### Usage

```
jira sprint remove <issue-key> [flags]
```

### Examples

```bash
jira sprint remove MYPROJ-42
```

---

## jira sprint create

Create a new sprint on a board.

### Usage

```
jira sprint create [flags]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Short | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--board` | `-b` | Board ID |
| `--name` | `-n` | Sprint name |
| `--goal` | `-g` | Sprint goal |
| `--start` | | Start date (ISO 8601, e.g. `2024-01-15`) |
| `--end` | | End date (ISO 8601) |

### Examples

```bash
jira sprint create --board 10 --name "Sprint 5" --goal "Ship auth module" \
  --start 2024-01-15 --end 2024-01-29
```

---

## jira sprint start

Start a future sprint.

### Usage

```
jira sprint start <sprint-id> [flags]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Short | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--start` | | Override start date |
| `--end` | | Override end date |

### Examples

```bash
jira sprint start 123
jira sprint start 123 --start 2024-01-15 --end 2024-01-29
```

## jira sprint close

Close (complete) an active sprint and move remaining issues to the backlog
or a specified target sprint.

### Usage

```
jira sprint close <sprint-id> [flags]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Short | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--move-to` | | Sprint ID to move incomplete issues to |
| `--confirm` | | Skip confirmation prompt |

### Examples

```bash
jira sprint close 123
jira sprint close 123 --move-to 124 --confirm
```
